مَزْعُوقٌ Frightened; as also ↓ زَعِيقٌ : (K:) [or frightened so as to be rendered brisk, lively, or sprightly, with fear:] see 1, in two places. [See also زَعِقٌ.] Applied to a colt, Frightened, and sharp in spirit: (S:) or, applied to a man, sharp in spirit: and, applied to a colt, well fed. (TA.) ―
-b2- أَرْضٌ مَزْعُوقَةٌ Land rained upon by vehement rain falling in large drops. (K, TA.) ＝
-A2- طَعَامٌ مَزْعُوقٌ Food having much salt put in it; (S, K;) as also ↓ زُعَاقٌ . (TA.) And قِدْرٌ مَزْعُوقَةٌ A cooking-pot in which much salt has been put. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
